id: # REPRESENTATION OF DATA TYPES - The Data Type Models in this Compiler

description: The compiler defines four distinct data representation models: (1) ABI representation for function calls, (2) SSA representation for MLIR operands, (3) Heap representation for runtime objects, and (4) Logical representation for Elm semantics
source: rules in one representation model do not imply rules in another unless explicitly stated

description: At all function call boundaries (kernel or compiled), every parameter and result whose monomorphized Elm type is Int, Float, or Char is passed and returned as a pass-by-value MLIR primitive (Int→i64, Float→f64, Char→i16), and every other Elm value including Bool and polymorphic type variables crosses the ABI as !eco.value regardless of its heap field representation
source: no ABI slot of type !eco.value may correspond to an Elm Int, Float, or Char.

description: ABI representation is independent of heap field representation
source: a value may be passed as a pass-by-value MLIR type at the ABI boundary while being stored boxed or unboxed in heap fields according to layout metadata

description: SSA operands use immediate MLIR operand types (i64, f64, i16, i1) only for Int, Float, and Char values
source: all other Elm values are represented as !eco.value, which denotes a heap pointer or an embedded constant
column7: SSA representation is independent of heap field layout and ABI calling conventions

description: At LLVM IR level every SSA value whose source type was !eco.value is ptr addrspace(1)
source: all crossings into i64 happen only at heap/global/closure/args storage boundaries and debugging helpers
column7: embedded constants are encoded as inttoptr of i64 constant to ptr addrspace(1). Sub-invariants: (a) REP_LLVM_PTR_ONLY_ACROSS_GC — no i64 derived from ptrtoint ptr<1> is live across a gc.statepoint
column8: (b) INT→PTR provenance — every inttoptr i64→ptr<1> result has an operand loaded from a GC-scanned slot or is an embedded-constant pattern
column9: (c) Boundary restriction — ptrtoint/inttoptr involving ptr<1> appears only at heap/global/closure storage boundaries args arrays and ADT case/tag bit-manipulation and embedded-constant encoding/decoding
column10: (d) Single-use i64 from ptrtoint — the i64 result is stored passed to a gc-leaf callee or consumed by bit-tests in the same basic block. Enforced post-RS4GC by EcoPtrIntVerify (ECO_GC_DEBUG_LIVENESS)

description: Heap object field representation is determined solely by layout metadata (RecordLayout, TupleLayout, CtorLayout) produced during monomorphization and is independent of ABI and SSA operand representation
Each unboxed slot carries a 2-bit kind (00=boxed HPointer, 01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char) at bits [2i, 2i+1] of the container bitmap
source: GC and debug logic must rely exclusively on this 2-bit kind or on constant bits in HPointer values to distinguish pointers from unboxed values (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

description: Projection from heap objects into SSA produces immediate MLIR operand values whose MLIR type matches the slot's 2-bit kind (01→i64, 10→f64, 11→i16)
source: kind=00 yields !eco.value (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

description: Construction of heap objects from SSA values sets per-slot 2-bit kinds based solely on SSA operand MLIR types (i64→01, f64→10, i16→11, else→00), and the runtime layout must match the bitmap exactly (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

For every monomorphized specialization and every eco.project.* op that reads a heap field (including list_head, tuple, record, and custom projections), the MLIR result type must be exactly the SSA type implied by the projected field’s MonoType: MInt→i64, MFloat→f64, MChar→i16, and all other types→!eco.value
source: in particular, eco.project.list_head on an MList elemType yields an immediate i64/f64/i16 result iff the element type is Int/Float/Char respectively, and !eco.value otherwise.

description: Closure objects capture values using SSA representation rules: immediate operands are stored with a 2-bit kind (01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char), Bool and all other values are stored as !eco.value (kind 00)
source: at most 26 typed captures fit in the 52-bit bitmap (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot

description: Closure application preserves captured value representation: 2-bit slot kinds are preserved across partial application extension
source: eco_pap_extend merges old and new bitmaps with a 2*old_n_values shift (Updated 2026-04-20: merge uses 2-bit-per-slot shift)

description: For every closure lambda FV(body) is a subset of params union captures union siblingMappings keys: all free variables in the body must be either parameters or explicitly captured or mutually-recursive siblings. Prevents missing captures and cross-function SSA leakage into lambda bodies
Every eco.papCreate with captures must have _fast_evaluator attribute referencing a valid function symbol with compatible signature
Closure calls with _dispatch_mode=fast require _fast_evaluator and _capture_abi attributes
source: the capture ABI types must match the fast clone parameter prefix

description: At control-flow merges (eco.case eco.if) closures with differing closure_kind values must result in _closure_kind=heterogeneous or absent
Every closure call must have _dispatch_mode attribute (fast closure or unknown)
_dispatch_mode=unknown indicates missing closure kind metadata and should trigger a diagnostic
source: in well-formed MLIR after full ABI analysis it should not occur

description: After ABI cloning each closure-typed parameter within a single function specialization has at most one capture ABI across all call sites
For every closure with captures the fast clone signature must be (capture_types ++ param_types) -> return_type and the generic clone signature must be (Closure* param_types) -> return_type
Zero-capture closures do not have _closure_kind _fast_evaluator or _generic_evaluator attributes
source: they reference the original lambda directly via the function attribute

description: Well-known constants such as Unit, True, False, Nil, Nothing, EmptyString, and EmptyRec are represented as HPointer values with nonzero constant bits and are never heap allocated
source: GC and debug logic must treat such values as non-heap and must not attempt to trace them

description: SSA values of type !eco.value may denote either heap pointers or embedded constants, and codegen, GC, and runtime helpers must rely on HPointer constant bits rather than pointer range checks to distinguish them
The only comparable embedded HPointer constants in Elm are Const_EmptyString ("") and Const_Nil ([])
source: both represent the minimum value of their type. Any compare/lt/le/gt/ge path that encounters one of these constants opposite a heap value of the same type must return LT for the constant-vs-heap case and GT for the heap-vs-constant case. Const_EmptyString must additionally compare EQ against any heap String with header.size == 0 in any string form (Tag_String / Tag_StringSlice / Tag_StringRope / Tag_LargeStringHeader). No other comparable embedded constants are planned
column7: the "two constants of different comparable families" case is unreachable under well-typed Elm.

id: # CANONICALIZATION PHASE - Resolve names, assign IDs, validate scopes

description: Every non-local variable reference in the canonical AST (top-level functions foreign imports constructors operators kernel vars) records its home module as an IO.Canonical so there is no ambiguity about which module a global name comes from while local variables are represented as VarLocal and resolved via the canonicalization environment

Every canonical expression node is assigned a unique non-negative integer ID ExprInfo.id by threading an Ids.IdState and calling Ids.allocId at each construction site and these IDs are later used as keys in the NodeTypes map returned by the type solver

No duplicate top-level value type constructor or port names exist in a module duplicates are detected via the Dups tracker and reported as DuplicateDecl DuplicateType DuplicateCtor DuplicateBinop or ExportDuplicate errors and shadowing of local bindings is likewise detected and reported as Shadowing

All imports must resolve to valid interfaces and all imported values types constructors and operators must come from those interfaces Foreign.createInitialEnv builds the environment from the given interface map and import list and unresolved or ambiguous imports yield canonicalization errors such as ImportNotFound ImportExposingNotFound or the various Ambiguous* errors

Module-level value definitions are partitioned into strongly connected components via Graph.stronglyConnComp this two-phase cycle detection (using all dependencies vs direct dependencies) ensures that groups used for type inference are valid recursive components and that non-terminating cyclic values are rejected with RecursiveDecl or RecursiveLet errors

Certain expression and pattern forms cache type information directly in the canonical AST to avoid interface lookups later in particular VarForeign VarCtor VarDebug VarOperator and Binop nodes carry cached Can.Annotation or Can.Type fields and constructor patterns PCtor and PatternCtorArg embed types for inference exhaustiveness checking and optimization

id: # TYPE CHECKING PHASE - Generate and solve constraints ensure type safety

description: In both erased and typed pathways type constraint generation traverses all declarations effects (ports and managers) expressions and patterns reachable from the module producing a single Constraint tree that encodes all required type relationships

Constraint solving uses union-find-based unification to compute consistent assignments for type variables and every unification failure produces a Type.Error (for example via Unify.AnswerErr and Error.BadExpr) that is propagated as a BadTypes error rather than silently corrupting the environment

After Solve.runWithIds completes every non-negative expression or pattern ID that was recorded during constraint generation has an entry in the nodeTypes dictionary (ExprTypes or NodeTypes) mapping that ID to a canonical type while negative placeholder IDs are intentionally skipped by the NodeIds.recordNodeVar helper

The occurs check implemented in Compiler.Type.Occurs is invoked by the solver during unification to detect and reject infinite types (such as a equals List a) and any such cycle results in a type error recorded in the solver state ensuring infinite types are never accepted

Let-bound type variables are ranked by lexical nesting depth using rank pools and generalization only quantifies variables at the appropriate rank promoting or freezing younger variables as needed thus implementing rank-based let-polymorphism and preventing unsound polymorphism from leaking across scopes

User-provided type annotations are canonicalized to Can.Annotation and inserted into the constraint tree the solver then enforces equality between annotated and inferred types so mismatches cause Type.Error values that surface as BadTypes errors rather than being silently ignored

In the typed constraint generator every type variable registered via NodeIds.recordNodeVar for an expression or pattern id must also appear in at least one constraint that participates in unification (either as the entire left or right side of a CEqual or nested inside a structured type that is unified)
source: a recorded variable that is only ever mentioned in NodeIds and never in any unification constraint indicates a missing constraint for that node and is treated as an internal compiler error

id: # NITPICK PHASE - Pattern exhaustiveness and other semantic checks

description: Every case expression is exhaustive after the Nitpick phase meaning all possible values of the scrutinee type are covered by at least one pattern and any missing patterns are reported as InexhaustivePatterns errors so downstream phases can assume case expressions always match exactly one alternative at runtime

id: # POST-SOLVE PHASE - Fix remaining Group B types (Str, Chr, Float, Unit) and infer kernel function types

description: The PostSolve phase walks the canonical AST after solving and assigns structurally computed types to remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) whose solver types were unconstrained synthetic variables deriving these types from known concrete types. Most expression forms (List Tuple Record Lambda Accessor Let LetRec LetDestruct) are now Group A with solver-owned types via recordNodeVar and do not need structural repair

Kernel function types are inferred by a two-step process seeding the kernel environment from alias definitions whose bodies are VarKernel expressions and then propagating types from usages (direct calls constructor arguments binary operators and case branches) using one-way scheme-to-type unification to build a KernelTypeEnv that maps (home name) kernel pairs to canonical function types with first-usage-wins semantics

After PostSolve all non-negative expression IDs in NodeTypes have meaningful concrete types and no unconstrained synthetic type variables remain for non-kernel expressions so the fixed nodeTypes map is guaranteed to be suitable for building TypedCanonical and for downstream typed optimization

For remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) the structurally computed PostSolve types depend only on the canonical AST structure and the initial solver-produced nodeTypes so given the same canonical module and initial nodeTypes PostSolve deterministically produces the same fixed nodeTypes and kernelEnv

For every non-negative expression/pattern node id whose solver-produced (pre-PostSolve) type is not a bare Can.TVar PostSolve must not change that node type (alpha-equivalent) except for VarKernel nodes whose types may be inferred/filled during PostSolve

For every non-negative expression/pattern node id (excluding VarKernel and Accessor nodes) the set of free Can.TVar names appearing in the node post-PostSolve type must be a subset of those appearing in its pre-PostSolve solver type ensuring PostSolve does not introduce new polymorphism

Every lambda expression in the canonical module has a concrete structural function type. Lambdas are now Group A (solver-owned via recordNodeVar) so the solver provides their type directly. PostSolve verifies that the stored type is alpha-equivalent to the recomputed structural type (TLambda chain from argument pattern types and body type) so lambdas never remain as bare TVars or non-function shapes.

For every lambda expression the set of free Can.TVar names appearing in its post-PostSolve type must be a subset of the type variables available in its surrounding solver environment (from its pre-PostSolve node type or enclosing annotated scheme) ensuring that PostSolve does not introduce new unconstrained lambda-local type variables and that all lambda polymorphism originates from the main solver.

PostSolve-generated placeholder TVars used for structural repair of remaining Group B expressions (Str Chr Float Unit) must not appear in function positions in the fixed NodeTypes map for non-kernel expressions so that all function types visible to TypedCanonical TypedOptimized and monomorphization are expressed solely in terms of solver- or annotation-derived type variables and are free of PostSolve-only placeholders. Most expressions are now Group A and do not receive PostSolve placeholders.

For every non-kernel expression or pattern node id i, let EnvTVars(i) be the set of type variables available in i’s typing environment (the union of binders from all enclosing annotated or inferred type schemes, including generalized let-bound definitions) and let FreeTVars(i) be the set of Can.TVar names occurring in the final post‑PostSolve nodeTypes[i] type
source: the invariant is that FreeTVars(i) is a subset of EnvTVars(i), and any Can.TVar that remains in nodeTypes[i] but does not come from EnvTVars(i) indicates a leaked internal solver variable or placeholder and is treated as an internal compiler bug

id: # TYPED OPTIMIZATION PHASE - Preserve and exploit types in optimized IR

description: Every TypedOptimized.Expr variant carries its Can.Type as the last constructor argument and the typeOf helper function simply pattern-matches on each variant to return that trailing type field for any expression

All pattern matches are compiled into decision trees (Decider structures) that operate over flat variable bindings and destructor paths so no nested patterns remain in the TypedOptimized IR and the resulting Decider trees are exhaustive by construction relying on earlier pattern exhaustiveness checking and the decision-tree completeness guarantees

The typed local graph TOpt.LocalGraphData always includes the full Annotations dictionary mapping definition names to their type schemes carried over from type checking so monomorphization and backends can look up top-level types without re-consulting interfaces or re-running inference

Typed optimization is designed to be type-preserving transformations such as inlining dead-code elimination and case-to-decision-tree compilation construct new TOpt.Expr nodes whose attached Can.Type matches the inferred type from TypedCanonical or nodeTypes propagating types via local rules like function type equals argTypes arrow bodyType and call type equals peeled result type of the function

Function expressions in TypedOptimized carry their full function type as a list of (Name Can.Type) parameter types plus a result Can.Type and the overall expression Can.Type is the corresponding curried TLambda chain enabling accurate arity computation and type-directed specialization in monomorphization
Every TypedPath.Unbox segment in a typed decision tree is annotated with a concrete canonical wrapper type that corresponds to a single‑constructor union marked Can.Unbox and has a single field
source: this concrete Can.Type must be ground (contain no free Can.TVar) so that downstream phases can resolve a unique runtime wrapper shape for each Unbox path.

id: # MONOMORPHIZATION PHASE - Specialize polymorphic functions to concrete types

description: MonoType encodes fully elaborated runtime shapes so concrete Elm instantiations of source types appear as MInt MFloat MList MTuple MRecord MCustom or MFunction and the only remaining use of generic type variables is via MVar with an attached Constraint such as CEcoValue or CNumber that does not require further type inference
At MLIR codegen time no MonoType may contain MVar with CNumber constraint in any reachable position and any such occurrence indicates a failed specialization compiler bug
Remaining MVar with CEcoValue constraint are allowed and their concrete source types never affect runtime layout or calling convention and are tracked only for comparison or debugging purposes
Every MonoNode whose MonoType is a function must be callable so it is either MonoTailFunc params body monoType or MonoDefine expr monoType where expr is MonoClosure closureInfo body monoType

Each specialization identified by Global plus MonoType plus optional LambdaId has a unique SpecId recorded in SpecializationRegistry every MonoVarGlobal that mentions that SpecId refers to exactly one MonoNode implementing that specialization and there are no missing or orphan entries in the registry for any used instantiation

RecordLayout and TupleLayout store fieldCount indices and a 2-bit-per-slot unboxedBitmap so field order indices and per-slot primitive kinds (00=boxed, 01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char) for records and tuples are completely determined by these layouts (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)
Record field access computes fieldIndex and isUnboxed from the record MonoType layout so MonoRecordAccess and MonoRecordUpdate always use indices and unboxing consistent with RecordLayout

Function call specialization unifies canonical function types with monomorphic argument types so immediate numeric types are fixed to MInt or MFloat and immediate mismatches are treated as monomorphization bugs

Polymorphic Debug kernel calls keep type variables as MVar by applying an empty substitution so their MonoType stays polymorphic and those type variables always have CEcoValue constraint and do not affect runtime layout or calling convention
MonoGraph is type complete and contains every type in the program including all aspects of those types such as all constructors for custom types stored in ctorLayouts

MonoGraph is closed and hygienic every MonoVarLocal refers to a binder in scope every MonoVarGlobal and SpecId refers to an existing MonoNode and after applying the specialization-pruning pass (MONO_022) there are no unreachable specializations in the registry or nodes

For every function or closure node the function MonoType flattened arity (computed by recursively peeling nested MFunction layers e.g. MFunction [a] (MFunction [b] c) has flattened arity 2) is at least as large as the parameter list length and all call sites supply arguments not exceeding that flattened arity so full and partial applications are always well formed and closures returning functions (nested lambdas) are valid
For each custom type every constructor has a CtorLayout whose field count ordering and 2-bit-per-slot unboxedBitmap match the constructor's fields
source: all construction and pattern matching nodes that use that constructor are consistent with its CtorLayout (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot
column7: Custom supports up to 24 typed slots)

description: Structurally equivalent record and tuple types share RecordLayout or TupleLayout identifiers or at least have layouts with identical indices and 2-bit-per-slot unboxedBitmap so layout metadata is canonical and does not spuriously duplicate equivalent layouts (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

When an accessor like .name with canonical type { ext | name : T } -> T is passed as a first-class function argument to a call site the accessor extension variable ext must be unified with the full record type inferred from other arguments at that call site so that specialization receives the complete record layout not just the explicitly named fields

For every SpecId in SpecializationRegistry.reverseMapping with value (global monoType maybeLambda) there exists a MonoNode at graph.nodes[specId] and monoType equals the nodeType of that node ensuring registry keys match actual node types

For every MonoCase expression in the MonoGraph the types of all branch expressions both in the jumps list and inline leaves in the decider must equal the MonoCase resultType ensuring consistent branch result types.
Within a single MonoGraph each lambdaId identifies a unique logical lambda
source: no two MonoClosure or MonoTailFunc nodes share the same lambdaId.

description: After monomorphization every user-defined local function or lambda (non-kernel) that is reachable from MLIR codegen has no MVar with CEcoValue constraint in its MFunction parameter or result positions. Remaining CEcoValue MVar in those positions indicates a failed specialization. Enforced structurally by collectLocalCallSubst which derives concrete type variable mappings from call sites before specializing the local definition.

After monomorphization and at MLIR codegen entry every reachable non-kernel user-defined function or closure specialization (reachable per MONO_022) has no MVar with CEcoValue and no MErased in its MFunction parameter or result positions. MErased replaces MVar in dead-value specializations (specValueUsed not set) and must not survive pruning into the reachable graph. Any remaining CEcoValue MVar is restricted to kernel-facing or metadata-only Mono nodes and unreachable template specializations are removed by MONO_022.

After monomorphization and specialization-pruning every SpecId in SpecializationRegistry.mapping or MonoGraph.nodes is reachable from the main specialization via the callEdges graph. The reachable set is the least fixed point starting from mainSpecId and following all MonoVarGlobal edges collected in callEdges. No unused template specializations remain in MonoGraph. CtorShapes are also pruned to only include types referenced by reachable nodes.

MErased in MonoTypes that reach MLIR codegen (monoTypeToAbi monoTypeToOperand processType) is mapped to !eco.value (boxed). MErased arises from dead-value specializations (eraseTypeVarsToErased) and phantom type variables in polymorphic-key specializations (eraseCEcoVarsToErased). It is semantically equivalent to CEcoValue and is always lowered as a boxed eco.value at all boundaries.

For every specialization entry in SpecializationRegistry whose key MonoType is fully monomorphic (contains no Mono.MVar with CNumber or CEcoValue constraint and no MErased) and is reachable after specialization-pruning (MONO_022), a traversal of all MonoTypes reachable from its implementing MonoNode (including function parameter types, closure capture types, local binding types, and expression result types such as MonoLet, MonoCase branches, and intermediate nodes) must find no remaining Mono.MVar with CEcoValue constraint
source: any surviving CEcoValue MVar in such a context indicates either an incorrectly computed specialization key or a failure to propagate call-site or context constraints into the monomorphization substitution for that specialization.

description: For every reachable MonoClosure or MonoTailFunc node implementing a user-defined function or lambda specialization, the closure’s stored MonoType must be consistent with its specialization key: reconstruct the canonical function type from the specialization key MonoType and the top-level type environment, apply the monomorphization substitution used for that specialization, convert the resulting canonical function type to a MonoType (preserving TLambda staging), and assert that the flattened parameter and result types match the closure’s parameter list and result type (up to currying structure) so that closure parameter types, capture layouts, and return types are guaranteed to reflect the same concrete instantiation as the specialization key.

For every TypedPath.Unbox segment produced by typed optimization, monomorphization computes a unique Mono.MonoType for the wrapper and selects a corresponding CtorLayout entry from MonoGraph.ctorLayouts (or typeRegistry.ctorShapes keyed by that MonoType)
source: MLIR codegen must use only this wrapper MonoType and its CtorLayout to determine field index, unboxed/boxed representation, and MLIR operand type for the unwrapped field, and may not consult global ctor shape lists or constructor names alone.

description: For every MonoVarGlobal(region specId monoType) reference in a reachable MonoNode the flattened function arity of monoType must equal the flattened function arity of nodeType(graph.nodes[specId]). A mismatch indicates that the specialization call site computed a truncated or otherwise incorrect function type for the referenced specialization typically caused by buildCurriedFuncType dropping unsupplied parameter stages during partial-application type construction. This invariant is checked after GlobalOpt since staging canonicalization may adjust node arities.

id: # GLOBAL OPTIMIZATION PHASE - Staging normalization and ABI consistency

description: For every MonoClosure with function type MFunction after GlobalOpt the length of closureInfo.params equals the length of stageParamTypes(monoType). This is established by canonicalizeClosureStaging and verified by TestLogic.Generate.MonoFunctionArity test suite. Monomorphize is staging-agnostic
source: GlobalOpt canonicalizes types to match param counts.

description: For every MonoCase after normalizeCaseIfAbi all branch result types equal the case result type including staging. The ABI normalization pass uses chooseCanonicalSegmentation to pick a common staging and buildAbiWrapperGO to wrap branches that differ.
After GlobalOpt every MonoCall has a non-placeholder CallInfo that reflects a staging decision for that call site
source: no call retains an unknown or default CallInfo.

description: For StageCurried calls CallInfo.stageArities encodes the full stage segmentation of the callee's canonical function type as a non-empty list of positive integers.
For StageCurried calls the sum of CallInfo.stageArities equals the total number of parameters in the callee's canonical flattened MFunction type.

For StageCurried calls that create or extend a partial application CallInfo.initialRemaining and CallInfo.remainingStageArities together describe exactly how many arguments remain to fully saturate the current closure stage and any subsequent stages in a way consistent with the callee's stageArities and the number of arguments supplied at this call site.

For StageCurried calls CallInfo.isSingleStageSaturated is true iff this call does not create or extend a partial application for the callee's current closure stage—that is after applying the provided arguments there is no remaining first-stage arity to carry forward.
For FlattenedExternal calls CallInfo encodes that there is no staged currying: callModel is FlattenedExternal and stageArities and remainingStageArities are empty with initialRemaining equal to zero
source: MLIR treats such calls as flat ABI calls.

description: ABI wrapper closures created by buildAbiWrapperGO and buildNestedCallsGO invoke their callees stage by stage according to the callee's segmentation
source: each nested MonoCall passes exactly the number of arguments for that stage and the result becomes the callee for subsequent stages. Verified by construction in buildNestedCallsGO and indirectly via CallInfo invariants GOPT_010-015.

id: # MLIR CODEGEN PHASE - Generate MLIR from monomorphized IR

description: MLIR codegen only inserts boxing and unboxing between immediate MLIR operand types and eco.value and any mismatch between different immediate MLIR operand types such as i64 versus f64 is treated as a monomorphization bug rather than fixed locally
generateCall treats calls whose result MonoType is still a function as partial applications and routes them through closure generation and eco.papExtend instead of emitting direct calls

Closure partial application and application ops (eco.papCreate, eco.papExtend) compute their unboxed bitmaps solely from SSA operand MLIR types after closure-boundary normalization: only unboxable primitives (i64, f64, i16) are marked unboxed and all other operands (including Bool/i1) are treated as !eco.value, and the _operand_types, unboxed_bitmap, and newargs_unboxed_bitmap attributes must exactly match the SSA operand types and layout used by the runtime

generateDestruct and generateMonoPath always use the destructor MonoType to determine the path target MLIR type and never use the body result type so destruct paths yield their natural type and do not spuriously unbox
generateMonoPath projects heap fields into SSA operands: when the 2-bit slot kind in the heap layout is non-zero the result is an immediate SSA operand of the matching primitive type (i64/f64/i16)
source: kind=00 yields !eco.value (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

description: generateLet binds let names directly to the SSA value and MLIR type of the defining expression without wrapping in eco.construct so variable bindings preserve original boxed or unboxed representation
boxToMatchSignature and boxToMatchSignatureTyped adjust call arguments only to satisfy ABI representation rules without changing heap layout or SSA operand representation
eco.construct eco.project eco.call and eco.return always carry an _operand_types attribute whose entries exactly match the MLIR SSA operand types used at that call site
Boolean constants may appear as i1 immediate SSA operands only in control-flow contexts (case scrutinees) and are otherwise represented as !eco.value constants at ABI, heap, and closure boundaries

Every eco.case is SSA value-producing: it has explicit MLIR result types on the op itself (not a result_types/caseResultTypes attribute), and every alternative region terminates with eco.yield whose operand arity and types exactly match the eco.case result types

Every function referenced by eco.call must have a corresponding func.func definition or declaration in the module so no undefined function symbols escape MLIR codegen and the UndefinedFunction pass validates this invariant by failing the build on any violation

monoTypeToMlir maps immediate MonoTypes to their unboxed MLIR types so MInt becomes i64 and MFloat becomes f64 and MChar becomes i16 and all other MonoTypes including MBool MVar and compound types become eco.value
At MLIR codegen time any MonoType component that is an MVar with CEcoValue constraint is always lowered to !eco.value so its concrete source type never affects generated layout or calling convention

MLIR codegen does not consult GlobalTypeEnv for union definitions and relies solely on MonoGraph.ctorLayouts for constructor metadata so all CtorLayout information is pre-computed during monomorphization and passed to MLIR codegen via the MonoGraph
monoTypeToMlir maps MChar to i16 (Eco_Char) not i32 and all codegen char constants and ops must use i16
List values are constructed only with eco.construct.list for Cons cells and eco.constant Nil for empty lists and never with eco.construct.custom
Tuples are constructed only with eco.construct.tuple2 for 2-tuples and eco.construct.tuple3 for 3-tuples and never with eco.construct.custom
Records are constructed with eco.construct.record when field_count is nonzero and empty records are always eco.constant EmptyRec and never heap allocated
Well known singleton values Unit True False Nil Nothing EmptyString and EmptyRec are always created via eco.constant and never via eco.construct or allocation

eco.construct.custom is used only for user defined custom ADTs and its tag size and 2-bit-per-slot unboxed_bitmap attributes and operand count match the CtorLayout selected from MonoGraph.ctorLayouts (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot
List destructuring uses eco.project.list_head and eco.project.list_tail only and never eco.project.custom or tuple or record projection ops
Tuple destructuring uses eco.project.tuple2 or eco.project.tuple3 with field index in range and never eco.project.custom or eco.project.record
Record field access uses eco.project.record with field_index in range and never eco.project.custom
Custom ADT field access uses eco.project.custom with field_index in range and no other projection op is used for custom ADT fields
All eco.construct.* operations produce !eco.value results regardless of whether any fields are stored unboxed
source: the SSA-only sibling family eco.make.* (eco.make.tuple2 eco.make.tuple3 eco.make.record eco.make.custom eco.make.cons eco.make.closure_env) instead produces a parameterised aggregate type (!eco.tuple2 etc.) and is introduced only by the EcoUnboxedAggSpecialize pass when escape analysis proves the value does not leave the function (Updated 2026-05-06 Phase 2)

description: For eco.construct.tuple2 eco.construct.tuple3 eco.construct.record and eco.construct.custom the unboxed_bitmap is derived solely from SSA operand MLIR types via encodeUnboxedKind
source: slot i occupies bits [2i, 2i+1] with kind 00=boxed, 01=i64 (Int), 10=f64 (Float), 11=i16 (Char) (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

description: For eco.construct.list the head_unboxed boolean is true iff the SSA head operand type is unboxable and the paired head_kind attribute encodes the 2-bit slot kind (00=boxed, 01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char) stored into cons->header.unboxed slot 0 (Updated 2026-04-20: head_kind attribute added alongside head_unboxed)
Every eco.case alternative region terminates with eco.yield and no alternative falls through past the end of a region
source: eco.return, eco.jump, eco.crash, and eco.unreachable are forbidden inside eco.case alternatives (except if nested under other non-eco.case regions that are never emitted directly by MLIR codegen)

description: eco.case tags array length equals the number of alternative regions
eco.jump target refers to a lexically enclosing eco.joinpoint with matching id and jump argument types match the joinpoint block argument types
Within a single func.func each eco.joinpoint id is unique to avoid joinpoint target ambiguity during lowering
_operand_types is required and must match SSA operand types when an op has one or more operands and may be omitted for zero operand ops
eco.papCreate requires arity greater than 0 and num_captured equals the number of captured operands and num_captured is less than arity

MLIR codegen emits eco.papExtend with !eco.value result type and produces immediate results only by inserting an eco.unbox after papExtend when the expected result type is an immediate MLIR operand type
Each module has at most one eco.type_table op at module scope
When eco.dbg carries arg_type_ids each referenced type id must refer to a valid entry in the module eco.type_table

eco.case scrutinee representation and case_kind agree: scrutinee is i1 only for boolean cases and scrutinee is !eco.value for ctor/int/chr/str cases and if case_kind is present it matches the scrutinee interpretation
All calls to the same kernel function name use exactly the same MLIR argument and result types across the whole module and any mismatch is a codegen bug

MLIR codegen does not emit eco.allocate eco.allocate_ctor eco.allocate_string or eco.allocate_closure and these allocation ops are introduced only by later lowering from eco.construct and related high level ops

For any operation that carries an `_operand_types` attribute, the attribute list length must equal the SSA operand count and each declared operand type must exactly match the corresponding SSA operand type (same order, no boxing/unboxing implied)
Within a module, all symbol definitions must be unique: no two `func.func` operations may have the same `sym_name` (and, more generally, no two symbol-bearing ops may define the same symbol)

Every block in every region emitted by MLIR codegen must end with a terminator operation (e.g. eco.return eco.jump eco.crash eco.unreachable eco.yield scf.yield cf.br cf.cond_br), and each eco.case alternative region must be properly terminated with eco.yield with no fallthrough past the end of the region

`eco.case` scrutinee representation and `case_kind` agree: `case_kind="bool"` requires an `i1` scrutinee, `case_kind="int"` requires an `i64` scrutinee, `case_kind="chr"` requires an ECO char scrutinee type, `case_kind="ctor"` requires a boxed `!eco.value` scrutinee, and `case_kind="str"` requires a boxed `!eco.value` scrutinee

Every `eco.call` callee must resolve to an existing `func.func` symbol in the module (definition or declaration), and calls must not target placeholder/stub implementations when a non-stub implementation is present (i.e. the selected callee must be the intended, non-trivial definition for that logical function)
eco.case is not a block terminator: it may appear mid-block as a value-producing expression op and its result SSA values may be used by subsequent operations in the same block

eco.case has no implicit control-flow exits: it always produces its results via eco.yield in exactly one selected alternative, and control continues in the enclosing block after the eco.case operation

Every decider region that becomes an eco.case alternative has a non-empty op list whose last op is eco.yield, and codegen never manufactures dummy eco.return terminators to "patch" unterminated decider regions
source: hitting a non-eco.yield tail in a case alternative is a codegen bug

description: The EcoControlFlowToSCF pass matches value-producing eco.case regardless of its position in a block, and rewrites it to scf.if or scf.index_switch by translating eco.yield terminators in alternatives to scf.yield and replacing the original eco.case results with the SCF op results
eco.papCreate and eco.papExtend unboxed_bitmap attributes are limited to 52 bits supporting at most 26 typed captures under 2-bit kind encoding
source: slot i kind at bits [2i, 2i+1] must match the i-th operand SSA type (kind 00 ↔ !eco.value, 01 ↔ i64, 10 ↔ f64, 11 ↔ i16) (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot

description: Lambda functions use typed signatures where capture parameters have their actual MonoType mapped to MLIR types and return types match the body expression type rather than always using eco.value so no internal boxing or unboxing is needed for immediate captures and returns
eco.papCreate arity attribute must equal the number of parameters that its referenced function symbol accepts so partial applications track the correct total arity

In typed mode (remaining_arity attribute present) eco.papExtend remaining_arity must equal the source PAP's remaining arity before this application (i.e. source's arity - num_captured for papCreate or previous remaining for chained papExtend) and must be >= num_new_args so the runtime can correctly determine whether the application is partial or saturated. In generic mode (remaining_arity absent) this invariant does not apply — saturation is determined at runtime from the closure header
eco.yield may only appear as the terminator of an eco.case alternative region and is forbidden in all other regions (including function bodies, joinpoint bodies, and SCF regions)
eco.return is forbidden inside eco.case alternative regions (eco.yield is the only legal case-alternative terminator) to prevent accidental non-local exits from within a value-producing case

When an ABI wrapper closure is created for a target segmentation [s1 s2 ...] the wrapper must have nested closure structure where the outermost closure has exactly s1 parameters (not the total flat arity) so that papCreate.remaining equals s1 and all case branches producing closures with the same staged type have identical papCreate.remaining values. This is a defense-in-depth check at MLIR level that depends on GOPT_001 being satisfied at the GlobalOpt level

For every typed-mode eco.papExtend (remaining_arity present) that represents a fully saturated closure application (isSaturatedCall) of some func.func @f, the eco.papExtend result MLIR type must equal the result type of @f's func.func signature. Generic-mode eco.papExtend (remaining_arity absent) always has !eco.value result type and this invariant does not apply.

Every kernel function symbol (Elm_Kernel_*) that appears in a papCreate papExtend or eco.call operation must have a corresponding func.func declaration with is_kernel=true and a function_type attribute whose parameter and result types match the ABI-level types computed by the Elm compiler from MonoType via monoTypeToAbi. Enforced by: (1) compiler registerKernelCall + generateKernelDecl at construction time (2) PapCreateOp and PapExtendOp verifiers hard-error on missing kernel declarations (3) UndefinedFunctionPass catches eco.call to undeclared symbols (4) EcoToLLVM getOrCreateWrapper fatal error on missing origFuncTypes entry for kernel functions

eco.papExtend in generic mode (no remaining_arity attribute) is the generic apply operation. EcoToLLVM lowers it by calling eco_apply_closure which reads the closure header (n_values/max_values) at runtime to determine saturation. Under-saturated returns a new PAP
column7: over-saturated chains stage evaluators recursively. Result type must be !eco.value. Typed closure calling attributes (_dispatch_mode _fast_evaluator _closure_kind) are ignored in generic mode

description: Generic-mode eco.papExtend (no remaining_arity attribute) is the generic apply operation. EcoToLLVM lowers it by building a typed i64* args buffer (no LLVM-side boxing of primitives) plus an EvalParamLayout describing each slot kind, then calling eco_apply_closure_typed. The runtime helper interprets the buffer per the layout (Int as i64, Float as bitcast f64, Char as zext i16, others as !eco.value HPointer) and is the single locus where any required re-boxing occurs
source: the LLVM IR for generic apply must not contain eco_alloc_int / eco_alloc_float / eco_alloc_char calls introduced solely to box arguments before the call.

description: eco_apply_closure handles over-saturated calls by chaining per-stage evaluators. When num_args > remaining (max_values - n_values) it saturates the current stage then recursively applies remaining args to the result closure. The intermediate result is a closure for the next stage with its own n_values/max_values header. GC safety is maintained because intermediate results are held in C stack locals

CallInfo.callKind determines the MLIR call lowering strategy. CallDirectFlat is used for FlattenedExternal (kernels/externs). CallDirectKnownSegmentation is used for StageCurried calls where the callee closure has a traceable body with known staging. CallGenericApply is used for StageCurried calls where the callee is dynamic, has polymorphic return, or has unknown evaluator ABI (MonoVarLocal or other non-global/non-kernel callee). CallSegmentationUnknown is used for StageCurried calls where the callee has known evaluator ABI (global or kernel) and known monomorphic ABI types but untrusted staging (sourceArityInfo = FromType or hasUnknownExcessArgs) and the callee is not dynamic and does not have polymorphic return

For eco.papExtend with _call_kind = segmentation_unknown remaining_arity must be absent. EcoToLLVM lowers the op by building a single typed i64* args buffer (no LLVM-side boxing of primitives) plus an EvalParamLayout describing each slot's ParamKind, then calling eco_apply_segmentation_unknown. The runtime helper reads the closure header to determine saturation and dispatches: under-saturated calls go to eco_pap_extend with a 2-bit-per-slot bitmap derived from the layout
source: saturated and over-saturated calls forward to eco_apply_closure_typed which centralises any required primitive re-boxing. The LLVM IR for segmentation_unknown apply must not contain eco_alloc_int / eco_alloc_float / eco_alloc_char calls introduced solely to box arguments before the call.

description: The SSA-only aggregate ops eco.make.tuple2 eco.make.tuple3 eco.make.record eco.make.custom eco.make.cons and eco.make.closure_env are Pure (NoMemoryEffect) and carry no live_roots operand: they materialise an LLVM struct value rather than allocating a heap object
source: eco.make.closure is the sole exception because it allocates a heap closure but uses a stack-allocated capture buffer of value-aggregate type

description: eco.to_heap accepts any aggregate type (!eco.tuple2 !eco.tuple3 !eco.record !eco.custom !eco.cons) as operand and produces a !eco.value heap pointer by allocating the corresponding heap object and copying fields
source: eco.to_heap explicitly rejects !eco.closure_env operands because closure environments only flow into eco.make.closure and never to the heap as standalone objects (verified by ToHeapOp::verify)

description: eco.from_heap is the inverse of eco.to_heap: it accepts an !eco.value HPointer and produces any data-aggregate type (!eco.tuple2 !eco.tuple3 !eco.record !eco.custom !eco.cons) by resolving the heap pointer once and loading each field at the corresponding heap-layout offset (Tuple2FirstOffset/Tuple3FirstOffset/RecordFieldsOffset/CustomFieldsOffset/Cons{Head,Tail}Offset). It is Pure (Elm heap immutability lets the load be reordered) and explicitly rejects !eco.closure_env results because closure environments are produced by eco.make.closure_env or read from the closure header, never by unboxing a heap aggregate (verified by FromHeapOp::verify)

Functions emitted by the Elm→MLIR generator carry eco.logical_param_types and eco.logical_result_types ArrayAttrs of StringAttr at every emission site that handles user-facing or inferable signatures (generateClosureFuncSingle generateClosureFuncWithClones generateTailFunc generateCtor generateEnum generateExtern generateManagerLeaf generateKernelDecl and the inline-lambda fast/$clo clones in Lambdas.generateLambdaFunc). Each entry is a small DSL string: "i64"/"f64"/"i16"/"i1" for primitives, "value" for !eco.value or any opaque/LUnknown shape, "tuple2:K0:K1" / "tuple3:K0:K1:K2" for tuples (K is i/f/c/v for i64/f64/i16/value), "record:N:K0:...:KN-1" for records in computeRecordLayout order, "custom:Tag:N:K0:...:KN-1" for single-constructor customs with N≤customMaxFields fields (multi-ctor and oversized customs encode as "value"), and "cons:Khead:Ktail" for list cons cells (tail is always "v" since List is recursive
source: cross-spec maps Cons to AggKind::None per Q4). Generic clones ($clo) encode the opaque closure pointer slot as "value". Both absent attributes and all-"value" shapes are treated by EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec as conservatively non-eligible (LUnknown clause)

description: EcoFlattenAggBoundary is the sole pass allowed to introduce multi-arg / multi-result func.func signatures derived from aggregate boundary types and is the sole pass that produces eco.flattened_boundary = unit attributes. It runs after EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec and the per-function escape-analysis / specialise passes
source: after it runs no value-aggregate type appears at any func.func boundary anywhere in the module — every aggregate-typed param/result has been split into N scalar params/results with eco.make.* / eco.project.* shims at the entry block (params) and at every func.return (results) and every func.call site of the flattened function. Cons and !eco.closure_env aggregate types are NOT flattened (Q4: Cons stays !eco.value at boundaries
column7: closure envs are Phase 4 scope). Phase 3.3 amendment: EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec is the only other source of new func.func parameters — it prepends one !llvm.ptr (addrspace 0) outparam per Sret-classified result on the worker's signature. Those leading outparams are !llvm.ptr never an aggregate type and therefore do not require flattening
column8: EcoFlattenAggBoundary observes them, ignores them at the boundary, and continues flattening any aggregate-typed params on the same worker as usual

description: Every func.func tagged eco.unboxed_worker whose signature contains an Sret outparam (a leading !llvm.ptr appearing before the worker's logical params) writes each field of the corresponding logical result via per-element llvm.getelementptr + llvm.store immediately before its func.return — no statepoint, no GC-may-call op, and no other side-effecting op may appear between the first sret store of any return and its terminator. This guarantees that the pointer the worker writes to the slot is the post-relocation form (whichever GC moves happen inside the worker have already settled), so the wrapper's subsequent llvm.load yields a valid ptr addrspace(1). Caller-side: the slot is allocated by llvm.alloca in LLVM addrspace 0 (host memory in the wrapper's stack frame), so RS4GC does not track it as a heap reference — it lives across the worker call as a normal SSA value whose pointee is the caller's frame. The loaded ptr addrspace(1) values become regular SSA pointers and are tracked through any subsequent statepoint (typically eco.construct.* in the wrapper's re-box step, or eco.to_heap elsewhere) via standard relocation rules

Worker functions produced by EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec carry the unit attribute eco.unboxed_worker. The pass uses this marker to skip already-specialised functions on re-entry and to identify workers in downstream passes. PAP/indirect-call conservatism is enforced implicitly via the per-param use check: any aggregate parameter whose uses include eco.papCreate eco.papExtend scf.while or non-eligible-callee call sites is demoted to Boxed before the worker signature is built so the wrapper retains the original ABI for closure-mediated callers. Phase 3.1 #5 extension: cross-spec runs a fixpoint analysis admitting calls to other already-eligible workers (the fixpoint loop iterates until no new functions are promoted)
source: call sites inside a worker body whose callee is in the eligible set are redirected to the callee's $unboxed worker (with eco.from_heap bridges where necessary) to avoid box/unbox round-trips in chained pipelines. Self-recursion (a single-node SCC with a self-edge) is allowed and handled in-place. Phase 3.2 #1 extension: a second analysis pass after the DAG fixpoint runs an inner per-SCC fixpoint over each multi-member SCC, admitting same-SCC calls as if the callee were eligible iff the callee's tentative slot shape matches the caller's at that position (verified via aggregateShapesMatch). Demotion in any member propagates through to every other member referencing that slot, so surviving shapes are mutually consistent by construction. Members commit independently once tentative shapes stabilise
column7: the existing CalleeRedirect machinery rewrites intra-SCC calls to the appropriate $unboxed worker (or leaves them on the wrapper for members with no promoted slots). Phase 3.3 extension (sret): for each aggregate result whose element list contains at least one !eco.value the worker signature drops that result from the LLVM return list and prepends a leading !llvm.ptr (addrspace 0) outparam in its place, in source order. Workers may mix Direct returns (all-primitive aggregates and scalars) with Sret outparams on the same function. Wrappers allocate the slot via llvm.alloca of a literal !llvm.struct<...> matching the aggregate's element layout (with !eco.value mapped to ptr addrspace(1)), pass the slot pointer as the leading operand to the worker call, then load each field back via per-element GEP+load and rebuild and re-box the aggregate via a single eco.construct.* op (the wrapper feeds the loaded sret-slot fields directly as construct operands
column8: no intermediate eco.make.* / eco.to_heap pair is built, so no register-form FCA exists in the wrapper). Intra-worker calls to other Sret-classified callees follow the same allocate-pass-load-rebuild pattern locally. The ABI choice is recorded on Candidate::resultAbis and CalleeRedirect::resultAbis and is derived from the result's element types (chooseResultAbi). Direct ABI is additionally capped at kMaxDirectFields elements (currently 3): all-primitive aggregates with more than kMaxDirectFields fields route through Sret rather than Direct because LLVM 21's SelectionDAG StatepointLowering asserts CallEnd != CALLSEQ_END (StatepointLowering.cpp:354) when lowering a gc.statepoint call whose result is a wide LLVM struct — the walker hits the CopyFromReg-per-field chain emitted by SelectionDAG between the call and CALLSEQ_END. Phase A empirical sweep (test/codegen/llvm-statepoint-struct-return-{N}.mlir) shows N=1..3 pass and N=4..8 assert
column9: the cap is the largest pass-count. Phase 3.4 #1 extension (join shapes as result producers): the result-side eligibility check accepts an aggregate return reached through `arith.select` (recursive on both arms) or `eco.case` (recursive on every alternative's matching `eco.yield` operand). Bottom-of-chain leaves stay the existing set (construct.*, from_heap, eligible/same-SCC call result, block-arg passthrough). The rewrite hoists the aggregate decomposition out of `eco.case` alternatives — each yield's aggregate operand is decomposed into N per-field projections, the `eco.case` is rebuilt with N scalar result types, and a single `eco.make.*` after the case rebuilds the aggregate. `arith.select` results are retyped in place. The `eco.case` widening (Eco_AnyValueOrAggregate result type) and `eco.yield`/`eco.return` operand widening flow through Ops.td. Walks both `func.return` and `eco.return` so Elm-generated function bodies (which terminate with `eco.return`) reach the same promotion path as hand-written codegen fixtures. Sret combined with eco.return on aggregates carrying `!eco.value` elements is allowed without an all-primitive gate: the wrapper's re-box is a single eco.construct.* op (rather than the eco.make.* + eco.to_heap pair used before plans/wrapper-fca-fix.md Fix A landed), and the Record/Custom eco.to_heap lowering pre-extracts every field before the alloc safepoint (Fix B), so RS4GC never sees an FCA over `ptr addrspace(1)` from the wrapper or the to_heap path. Phase 3.4 #2 (eco.joinpoint loop-carry support) is deferred — the use-check + rewrite would walk the joinpoint body, every eco.jump's matching operand, and the continuation block-args

description: Aggregate value types (!eco.tuple2 !eco.tuple3 !eco.record !eco.custom !eco.cons !eco.closure_env) are SSA-only by default: they participate in MLIR SSA dataflow and lower to LLVM struct types of i64/f64/i16/ptr addrspace(1) elements. They are introduced only by EcoUnboxedAggSpecialize (intra-function) and EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec (cross-function, Phase 3) and are eliminated by SROA before RewriteStatepointsForGC so RS4GC never sees a struct-typed gc pointer for intra-function values. Phase 3.1 amendment: aggregate types ARE temporarily permitted on func.func parameter and result types on functions tagged eco.unboxed_worker = true, but ONLY between EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec and EcoFlattenAggBoundary in the pipeline
source: after EcoFlattenAggBoundary runs no aggregate type appears at any func.func boundary anywhere in the module (each aggregate boundary slot is split into N scalar slots with eco.make.* / eco.project.* shims at entry and at call sites). This removes the FCA constraint on parameter aggregates (pre-3.1 they had to be all-primitive) — the flattened LLVM signature carries only scalars and pointers, so RS4GC never sees a struct-typed gc pointer at a call boundary. Phase 3.3 amendment: aggregate results containing at least one !eco.value element are also eligible — they use the sret ABI (CGEN_064 Phase 3.3 clause). The wrapper's slot alloca lives in LLVM addrspace 0 (host memory in the wrapper's stack frame) and holds a literal !llvm.struct<...> whose elements are the post-conversion LLVM types (with !eco.value mapped to ptr addrspace(1)). No struct value containing a ptr addrspace(1) crosses the worker call boundary — the worker takes the slot as a plain !llvm.ptr and stores fields scalar-by-scalar, so RS4GC's FCA-unimplemented assertion is structurally avoided. All-primitive aggregate results with up to kMaxDirectFields elements (currently 3) continue to use the Direct LLVM multi-return path (RS4GC tolerates struct returns whose elements are all scalars). Wider all-primitive aggregates route through Sret instead — see CGEN_064 for the SelectionDAG StatepointLowering bug that forces the cap. Phase 1 widen-construct-make-call-aggregates amendment: aggregate-typed SSA values may appear as operands of construct.* (tuple2/tuple3/list-head/record/custom), make.* (tuple2/tuple3/record/custom/cons/closure_env), and eco.call after EcoUnboxedAggCrossSpec promotes a callee's result type. The dedicated EcoBoxAggregateOperands pass (between EcoFlattenAggBoundary and EcoGCPrepare) walks these ops and inserts eco.to_heap in front of every aggregate operand at a boxed sink (construct.* / eco.call — unconditionally
column7: make.* — only when the aggregate's type recursively contains a !eco.value, since otherwise the inner aggregate nests as a flat FCA element in the outer SSA struct without bringing a ptr addrspace(1) inside a nested FCA). EcoGCPrepare then sees the new eco.to_heap ops as ordinary GCRootCarrier allocators and computes their root sets and adjacent-alloc grouping normally. The fuller story — recursive cross-spec ABI promotion plus recursive strip-aggregates so even GC-pointer-inner make.* cases stay un-boxed — is deferred to Phase 2 of the same plan

description: The compiler is the sole arbiter of kernel ABI types: kernelBackendAbiPolicy together with monoTypeToAbi computes the definitive MLIR types for all kernel function parameters and return values, func.func declarations with is_kernel=true carry these types, and the LLVM lowering pass (EcoToLLVM) reflects them without repair or reverse-engineering. In particular: (1) kernelBackendAbiPolicy must respect REP_ABI_001 so that any kernel parameter or result whose MonoType is MInt, MFloat, or MChar uses the corresponding primitive ABI type (i64, f64, i16) and is never lowered as !eco.value
source: (2) for AllBoxed kernels with polymorphic return types the call result type must be eco.value regardless of the monomorphized type because the C++ function always returns uint64_t.

id: # RUNTIME HEAP PHASE - Memory layout and GC invariants

description: Every heap object begins with an 8 byte Header struct and the first TAG_BITS bits of the header encode the Tag which denotes the concrete heap object kind
All heap objects are 8 byte aligned and getObjectSize always rounds object sizes up to a multiple of 8 bytes
GC and helper routines interpret heap object layout solely via Header.tag using a switch on the Tag enum in getObjectSize and related tracing functions
When introducing a new heap object type you must update the Tag enum the C plus plus struct definition getObjectSize scanObject and markChildren so all GC logic stays consistent with the Tag
There are no old to young pointers in the heap which is guaranteed by Elm immutability so the GC does not require a write barrier
Forwarding pointers use Tag_Forward and repurpose the header to store a logical pointer to the new location and they exist only during GC and never while mutator code runs
Each heap region is owned by exactly one ThreadLocalHeap so there are no cross thread heap pointers and each mutator collects only its own heap
All heap pointers are HPointer values whose ptr field is a 40 bit offset from heap_base so logical pointers are not raw addresses and only conversion helpers touch heap_base
HPointer is the canonical type for heap references and code must use fromPointer and toPointer or Allocator wrap and resolve rather than treating HPointer as a void star
Common constants such as Unit EmptyRec True False Nil Nothing and EmptyString are represented by nonzero HPointer.constant tags and never allocated as heap objects
Any allocation via ThreadLocalHeap allocate or Allocator allocate may trigger a minor GC which can move all live nursery objects so callers must assume heap locations may change across allocation
isInHeap uses an O(1) bounds check against heap_base plus heap_reserved so any pointer in the unified heap address range is treated as a potential heap object irrespective of generation

When allocating a heap object the Tag passed to Allocator allocate must correspond to the concrete struct written at that address because GC size and tracing logic derive layout solely from Header.tag
HPointer values with constant not equal to zero represent embedded constants and allocator and resolve operations must treat such pointers as non heap values that do not require tracing

For every heap allocation the header tag and in-memory layout must match the concrete runtime type such as Tuple2 Cons Record or Custom and no value of type List Tuple or Record is ever represented using the Custom struct because the tag and structure must always match

All eco_alloc_* runtime functions return uint64_t representing HPointer with constant field equal to 0 for heap objects and all functions receiving heap objects take uint64_t and use Allocator resolve internally to convert to raw pointers

Elm never produces null pointers so any allocation returning null indicates an out of memory condition and any HPointer with ptr equals 0 and constant equals 0 is a valid heap pointer to offset 0 not a null sentinel

Elm values are always acyclic because Elm is a pure functional language with immutable data and no recursive let bindings so any traversal of a value graph is guaranteed to terminate and runtime operations like debug printing may safely follow nested references without cycle detection
Container heap objects such as Custom Cons ElmArray and Record store a 2-bit-per-slot unboxed bitmap (00=boxed HPointer, 01=Int, 10=Float, 11=Char) with slot i at bits [2i, 2i+1]
source: GC and debug logic must use this bitmap to distinguish pointers from unboxed values and to select the correct primitive type (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

id: # BYTES FUSION REIFICATION PHASE - Static analysis and fusion eligibility

description: Reification is all-or-nothing and a fused kernel is emitted only when the entire encoder or decoder structure can be statically resolved otherwise the interpreter path is used
Dynamic encoders and decoders are rejected from fusion and any encoder or decoder whose structure depends on runtime values causes fallback to the interpreter
Let-bound encoders and decoders are reified only if fully resolvable at compile time and partially resolvable let bindings cause the entire fusion to be rejected
Reification preserves operation order exactly so the sequence of encode or decode steps in the fused kernel matches the order specified in the source program
Reification inspects structure only and never runtime values so fusion decisions are based solely on the static shape of the encoder or decoder AST

id: # BYTES FUSION OPS PHASE - bf dialect IR and lowering invariants

description: Cursor is the only mutable state in fused byte operations and all state flows through cursor threading with no hidden side channels
Cursor is SSA-threaded so every bf operation that modifies cursor state consumes the old cursor and produces a new cursor value
Cursor pointer movement is monotonic and the pointer only moves forward never backward during encoding or decoding
Cursor end pointer never changes during execution and is set once at cursor initialization from buffer allocation
Cursor invariant ptr less than or equal to end always holds and any violation indicates a bounds check failure
Width computation is exact and equals the sum of all emitted write widths so buffer allocation matches total write size
Exactly one buffer allocation occurs per encoder invocation and all writes go to that single buffer
No writes occur after the buffer is returned and ReturnBuffer is always the final operation in an encoder
Write order is preserved exactly and bytes appear in the output buffer in the same order as the source program specifies
Writes never exceed allocated buffer size because width computation guarantees exact allocation
No intermediate buffers are created during encoding and all writes go directly to the final output buffer
No load occurs without a prior successful bounds check so all reads are proven safe before execution
Bounds safety is structural and enforced by IR shape so the bf dialect structure guarantees checks precede loads
Failure is terminal and decoding exits immediately upon any bounds check or semantic failure
Cursor does not advance on failure so failed decode attempts leave the cursor at the failure position
Semantic failures propagate as Nothing through the Maybe result type and never as exceptions or traps
Decoder never throws or traps and all error conditions result in Nothing return values
Successful fused decode produces results identical to the interpreter so fusion is purely an optimization
Loop IR contains no raw pointers and all buffer access is mediated through cursor abstractions
Loop IR is cursor-based and all read and write positions are expressed as cursor states not pointer arithmetic
bf.cursor type is opaque above LLVM lowering and its internal structure is hidden from higher-level IR
bf operations have no side effects except cursor transformation and buffer mutation so they are pure with respect to external state
Control flow is explicit in IR and all branches and loops are represented as first-class control flow constructs
Operation order is expressed by SSA dependencies so the IR structure encodes execution order constraints
bf.cursor lowers exactly to LLVM struct containing ptr and end pointer pair with no additional fields
No speculative loads are generated and all loads are guarded by prior bounds checks in the CFG
Pointer arithmetic in lowered code matches cursor semantics exactly with no off-by-one errors or alignment issues
End pointer is computed once at cursor initialization and reused for all bounds checks without recomputation
Loads are dominated by bounds checks in the CFG so no execution path can reach a load without passing through its guard
Generated code never accesses runtime heap headers directly and all layout knowledge is encapsulated in runtime helpers
All heap objects cross the ABI boundary as eco.value and generated code does not assume internal pointer representations
Runtime helpers are the only layout-aware code and all ByteBuffer and String structure access goes through elm_bytebuffer_* and elm_utf8_* functions
Runtime helpers are thin and non-duplicative with each helper performing exactly one layout-aware operation
ABI stability is preserved across versions so compiled fused kernels remain compatible with runtime updates
Fused kernel contains exactly one loop for looped decoders with no nested iteration or recursive calls
No intermediate allocations occur during fused encode or decode and only the final result is heap allocated
No interpreter calls occur inside fused kernel and all operations are inlined as native LLVM IR
Fusion success is deterministic and predictable based solely on static structure so identical source programs always produce identical fusion decisions

id: # CROSS-PHASE INVARIANTS - Constraints spanning multiple phases (always last)

description: RecordLayout TupleLayout and CtorLayout from the monomorphized IR must agree with eco.construct attributes tag size and 2-bit-per-slot unboxed_bitmap and with the Custom and Record C plus plus structs so that MLIR objects match runtime layouts
source: Elm-side encodeUnboxedKind and runtime fieldKind must use the same encoding (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)

description: All !eco.value SSA operands produced by codegen must correspond to valid HPointer values (heap pointers or embedded constants) that satisfy runtime heap alignment and header invariants
MLIR code generation treats CallInfo on each MonoCall as the single source of truth for call staging and call model
source: it does not re-derive stage segmentation or call model from MonoTypes independently of GlobalOpt.

description: Between Monomorphization and GlobalOpt MonoTypes are preserved up to MFunction staging canonicalization
source: GlobalOpt may flatten nested function types to match closure parameter counts but may not otherwise change types or layout metadata.

id: # FORBIDDEN INVARIANTS - What not to do

description: No phase may assume that an SSA operand of immediate MLIR operand type corresponds to an unboxed slot in any heap object or closure unless the 2-bit slot kind from the explicit layout bitmap is consulted (Updated 2026-04-20: bitmap now encodes 2-bit primitive kinds per slot)
No phase may assume that a value passed as a pass-by-value MLIR type at an ABI boundary is stored as an unboxed field in heap objects or closures
No phase may assume that SSA operand representation implies ABI calling convention or vice versa except where explicitly specified by REP_ABI invariants
No code may distinguish heap pointers from constants using address range checks or null tests
source: only HPointer constant bits and header tags may be used

description: No code may perform arithmetic on HPointer values except via allocator helpers or runtime APIs
No phase may assume that Bool values are captured, stored, or passed as immediate operands outside SSA control-flow contexts
source: Bool must be represented as !eco.value in heap and closures

description: No phase may infer closure capture layout from MonoType or source type alone
source: layout must be derived from SSA operand MLIR types and recorded bitmaps

description: No code may assume a heap object’s field layout based solely on its Tag without consulting the corresponding layout metadata
No phase may assume that two structurally equal source types share layout unless their RecordLayout or TupleLayout identifiers are equal or explicitly canonicalized
No optimization may remove boxing or unboxing operations unless representation equivalence is proven under the active representation model
No generated code may access heap object internals directly except inside designated runtime helpers
No control-flow construct may assume implicit fallthrough
source: all region exits must be explicit terminators, and all eco.case alternatives must explicitly terminate with eco.yield

description: Debug and inspection code must not assume access to raw heap layouts and must use the same tracing logic as GC
No phase may rely on representation properties that are not explicitly stated in a REP_* invariant

Stackmap-derived stack roots and runtime/kernel roots are stored in disjoint containers: StackMapRoots (owned by ThreadLocalHeap, GC-internal) holds single-slot roots discovered from LLVM stackmaps and is cleared at the start of each GC cycle, while RootSet (owned by NurserySpace) holds long-lived roots, JIT roots, shadow-stack ranges, and external scanners. Cross-container mutation is prohibited
Runtime and kernel code must not register GC roots via the stackmap root container
source: all non-stackmap stack rooting must use RootSet::stack_root_ranges via StackRootGuard, StackRootRangeGuard, or the eco_gc_stack_range_* C ABI

description: Free cells in the old generation use Tag_Free with header.size storing the cell's full byte count (8-byte aligned). Free cells are never marked, scanned for children, or fixed by reference fixup
source: sweep, lazy sweep, mark, and compaction walks must skip them based on tag (Added 2026-04-24)

description: HeapConfig::initial_old_gen_size must be a multiple of alloc_buffer_size. The initial region is committed once via Allocator::acquireOldGenRegion and sliced into pages stored in OldGenSpace::unassigned_blocks_ at OldGenSpace::initialize time (Added 2026-04-24)

Mutator allocations in the old generation route through the segregated-fits + BBoP path: small/medium fixed-cell classes for size < classToSize cap, page-as-single-cell + split for [largest medium class, alloc_buffer_size), and dedicated pinned blocks via allocateLargeBlock for size >= alloc_buffer_size. Bump-pointer allocation survives only inside compaction's evacuation destinations (Added 2026-04-24)

Sweep and reference-fixup walks parse a block over [BlockInfo.start, BlockInfo.end_of_objects). Pages in OldGenSpace::unassigned_blocks_ are unparseable and must not be walked. end_of_objects is set to BlockInfo.end for fully-populated pages and to the bump frontier for evacuation-destination blocks (Added 2026-04-24)

If a TOpt.Meta has a polymorphic tipe (contains any Can.TVar) then meta.tvar must be Just and that variable must appear in the solver snapshot. Monomorphic synthetic nodes may have tvar=Nothing. Violations crash in MonoDirect with a clear internal error

All monomorphization decisions in MonoDirect are derived from the SolverSnapshot. specializeDefineNode must not have a fallback path that creates substitutions independent of the solver. Internal use of TypeSubst in SolverSnapshot.buildLocalView is acceptable as a deterministic projection of solver state

String values are heap-represented in four forms: Tag_String (flat UTF-16 leaf), Tag_StringRope (concat-tree node: HPointer left + HPointer right + u32 height + u32 leafCount), Tag_StringSlice (structural view: HPointer base + u32 offset + u32 length), and Tag_LargeStringHeader (split-header form, see HEAP_026). For all four, header.size = logical UTF-16 length. Compiler/MLIR allocation paths produce only Tag_String leaves directly
source: rope/slice nodes arise only in runtime String operations (StringOps and kernel String module). Tag_LargeStringHeader is produced transparently by alloc::allocString when total payload >= large_header_split_threshold. All structure access outside StringOps and elm_utf8_* must go through Elm::StringOps APIs (length, charAt, toStdString, toStdU16String, ensureFlat) or through HeapHelpers::stringLength/isString. stringData() resolves through Tag_LargeStringHeader to its body and asserts the resolved object is a Tag_String leaf. append/concat/join build ropes when total > FLATTEN_LIMIT
column7: equal/compare flatten under FLATTEN_LIMIT and fall back to char-by-char above (Updated 2026-05-01: added Tag_LargeStringHeader)

description: Strings/byte buffers whose total payload size meets or exceeds HeapConfig::large_header_split_threshold are represented by a small Tag_LargeStringHeader / Tag_LargeByteHeader (16 bytes: Header + HPointer body) in the nursery whose `body` HPointer references a Tag_String / Tag_ByteBuffer object pinned in old gen (header.pin = 1). Bodies are pointer-free and never copied. Bodies of nursery-owned headers are reclaimed at the end of any minor GC whose header-evacuation phase did not encounter the header — driven by a per-body 1-bit "seen this minor GC" color tracked in OldGenSpace::large_bodies_. On promotion of the header to old gen, OldGenSpace::promoteLargeHeader removes the body from nursery_owned_bodies_, transferring it to standard major-GC management. Major GC traces Tag_LargeStringHeader / Tag_LargeByteHeader by marking the body via markChildren. The body HPointer is a young->old reference (HEAP_005-compliant: that direction is always allowed). Bodies are reclaimed in all GC phases except compaction (sweepNurseryLargeBodies defers only when compact_phase_ != Idle)
source: during major-GC mark/sweep, freeLargeBodyCell installs the on-free-list sentinel on the resulting Tag_Free cell (HEAP_027) so the in-progress lazy sweep cannot coalesce or rewrite it. freeLargeBodyCell is the authoritative ownership transition for split-header bodies
column7: large_body_index_.erase calls in major sweep are idempotent guards only (Added 2026-05-01

description: Old-gen Tag_Free cells repurpose Header.age as an on-free-list sentinel. age & 0b01 == 1 means the cell is already linked into a size-class free list (placed there by freeLargeBodyCell during a mid-major-GC large-body reclaim)
source: the lazy-sweep coalescer treats such cells as hard run boundaries — it must not coalesce across, must not rewrite the header, and must not touch the free-list link. age & 0b01 == 0 means an ordinary coalescable Tag_Free cell. age & 0b10 is reserved for future use and must remain 0 in Tag_Free cells. Legal age values for Tag_Free are exactly 0 and 1. Producers of sentinel cells: freeLargeBodyCell (regular-block path) only. All other Tag_Free writers (pushCoalescedFreeCell from sweep, pushSpanOnFreeLists from bag-page splitting, padCellSlack trailing, populateFromBlock uniform slicing, freeLargeBodyCell is_large branch) write age=0. The 8-byte heap-base sentinel installed by installHeapBaseSentinel is EXEMPT from the convention
column7: it carries age=0 and is identified by address via isHeapBasePage not by the age bit. Garbage-bytes accounting for sentinel cells lives at the freeLargeBodyCell call site and is NOT re-applied by sweep (Added 2026-05-04)

description: Heap objects with Header.builder == 1 must reside in the nursery. Promotion to old gen is forbidden while the bit is set: the canonical promotion predicate is !pin && !builder && age >= promotion_age. Any old-gen object observed with builder == 1 is a kernel bug
While Header.builder == 1, Header.age must remain 0. mark_as_builder writes both bit=1 and age=0 atomically
source: minor-GC evacuation skips the new_hdr->age++ increment when builder == 1 in NurserySpace::evacuate, evacuateJitPtr, and evacuateListSpine. The invariant builder ⇒ age == 0 holds at every GC-visible point and is asserted under ECO_HEAP_VALIDATE on the to-space copy (Added 2026-05-10)

description: Runtime kernels that allocate via allocArrayBuilder (or otherwise set Header.builder = 1) must clear the bit via clear_builder / BuilderGuard destructor before the object becomes reachable to user Elm code. The standard idiom is allocArrayBuilder + scoped BuilderGuard so RAII guarantees clearing on every kernel exit (return, exception, early break) (Added 2026-05-10)
